candidate_relations.label: Cardiomyopathy with poor diastolic function
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture is dominated by markedly elevated troponin T (2230 ng/L), CK/CK-MB elevation, CMR evidence of myocardial edema and late gadolinium enhancement, and temporal association with sintilimab (PD-1 inhibitor) chemotherapy/immunotherapy cycles. This constellation defines immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis. 'Cardiomyopathy with poor diastolic function' is a broader, non-specific label that neither captures the inflammatory etiology (myocarditis) nor the specific causative agent (sintilimab/ICI), and diastolic dysfunction is merely one incidental finding on echo. The candidate conflicts in subtype (cardiomyopathy vs. myocarditis) and omits the required ICI-induced etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Describes a structural/functional cardiac category without specifying immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis as the etiology or subtype

case_quality_flags: Sintilimab is a PD-1 inhibitor; ICI-induced myocarditis is well-supported by CMR findings, markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers, and temporal relationship to immunotherapy cycles
Coronary CTA normal excludes ischemic etiology, strengthening myocarditis diagnosis
